card: Configures Guix to build Linux x86_64 and aarch64 release binaries (excluding the GUI) as `-static-pie` executables against glibc 2.44. This allows official Linux release binaries to run out of the box on non-glibc systems (such as Alpine Linux) and distributions running older glibc releases without dynamic linker dependencies. The PR author notes that static glibc linking disables dynamic NSS modules like mDNS, LDAP, and SSSD, and closes issue #19075 by enabling standard branch protection on aarch64. Depends on #36272 and #36193.
evidence: PR release notes: "Release binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux (except for bitcoin-qt) are now compiled with `-static-pie`, making them more portable. They can now be run on non-glibc based systems, as well as on systems than ship with older glibcs, than were previously supported."
PR description: "Using glibc for static builds, would be less of a leap compared to switching to musl libc (POC in #23203). Also fixes #19075."
problem: Linux release binaries dynamically link against glibc, which prevents them from running on distributions with older C libraries or non-glibc systems like Alpine Linux. Dynamic linking also complicates deploying self-contained binaries across diverse Linux environments.
scope_notes: Much of the diff consists of extracting toolchain build definitions from `manifest_build.scm` into a new `toolchains.scm` module, alongside glibc patches for deterministic store path remapping and disabling dynamic NSS library loading.
summary: Configure Guix to build non-GUI Bitcoin Core release binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux as static position-independent executables (`-static-pie`) using GCC and glibc 2.44. Move toolchain definitions into dedicated Guix modules and update `symbol-check.py` and `security-check.py` to handle static ELFs. Patch glibc to strip `/gnu/store` references and prevent runtime `dlopen` calls in NSS.
